The two-dimensional measurement method for the distance between the mandibular foramen and the upper incisor. A1: the upper incisor tip, A2: the upper incisor apex, L1: the lower incisor tip, L2: the lower incisor apex. K: the mandibular foramen. b: the distance between the upper incisor tip and the mandibular foramen. c: the distance between the lower incisor tip and the mandibular foramen. The distance between the upper and lower incisor tips and the mandibular foramen was measured. A1 and A2 were divided by the distance between the upper and lower incisor tips, respectively, to get ratio a. L1 and L2 were divided by the distance between the upper and lower incisor tips, respectively, to get ratio b. The distance between the mandibular foramen and the upper incisor apex was measured. The distance between the mandibular foramen and the lower incisor apex was measured. The ratio of the distance between the mandibular foramen and the upper incisor apex and the upper incisor apex was divided by the ratio of the distance between the mandibular foramen and the lower incisor apex and the lower incisor apex to get ratio c. The ratio of ratio a and ratio b was divided by the ratio of ratio b and ratio c to get the index.

Anteroposterior radiograph of the pelvis showing the 6-line measurement technique for acetabular offset (AO) ratio. Line 1: connecting the most medial point of the femoral head base and the most lateral point of the acetabulum. Line 2: connecting the most medial point of the femoral head base and the most lateral point of the femoral neck. Line 3: connecting the most medial point of the femoral head and the most lateral point of the acetabulum. Line 4: connecting the most medial point of the femoral head and the most lateral point of the femoral neck. Line 5: connecting the most medial point of the femoral head base and the most medial point of the femoral neck. Line 6: connecting the most lateral point of the femoral head base and the most lateral point of the femoral neck. The AO ratio is calculated as the percentage difference between the distance between the most medial point of the femoral head base and the most lateral point of the femoral neck (d1) and the distance between the most medial point of the femoral head base and the most lateral point of the femoral acetabulum (d2). AO ratio = (d1/d2) * 100%

Measurement of ankle alignment: M = medial, L = lateral, A = anterior, B = posterior, JL = joint line.

Measurement of the ankle joint angle (AJA) in the lateral view. The JL point is set at the center of the lateral malleolus and the CS point is set at the inferior corner of the medial malleolus. The angle formed by the lines connecting the JL and CS points is the AJA.

Illustration of the measurement of the JLD on an weight-bearing lateral radiograph of the left ankle. The JLD is defined as the distance between the point A (the most anterolateral point of the talar neck) and the point B (the most anteromedial point of the talar neck). The line connecting A and B is the JLD line. The JLD is determined by adding 0.5 cm to the horizontal distance between the inferior margin of the calcaneal protuberance (L) and the most lateral point of the talar neck (M). The JLD line is divided into three sections. JLD is measured as the sum of the distances between the most lateral point of the talar neck and the most lateral point of the calcaneal protuberance (JL), the most medial point of the talar neck and the most medial point of the calcaneal protuberance (JL), and the most lateral point of the talar neck and the most lateral point of the calcaneal protuberance (JL).

Determination of the lateral collateral ligament length (JL) and medial collateral ligament length (CS). The lateral collateral ligament was measured as the length between the tip of the lateral malleolus and the tip of the medial malleolus, and the medial collateral ligament was measured as the length between the medial malleolus on the lateral side of the lateral malleolus and the medial malleolus on the medial side of the medial malleolus.

The angle β is defined as the angle between the line connecting the first cervical vertebra and the second cervical vertebra and the line connecting the second cervical vertebra and the fifth cervical vertebra. The angle δ is defined as the angle between the line connecting the first cervical vertebra and the second cervical vertebra and the line connecting the second cervical vertebra and the fifth cervical vertebra. The angle α is defined as the angle between the line connecting the first cervical vertebra and the second cervical vertebra and the line connecting the second cervical vertebra and the fifth cervical vertebra.

The solid component of the mass was located in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen, which was 5 cm away from the upper pole of the right kidney. The solid component of the mass was connected with the right kidney, and the contrast agent was seen in the right renal pelvis on the post-contrast T1-weighted image. A 3-cm mass was observed in the left upper quadrant of the abdomen, which was located 6 cm away from the left kidney. The mass was homogeneously enhanced, and the mass was 1.5 cm away from the abdominal wall. The solid component of the mass was connected with the left kidney, and the contrast agent was seen in the left renal pelvis on the post-contrast T1-weighted image. The knee joint was segmented and the knee joint angle (KJA), patellar height (PH), patellar height ratio (PHR), and tibial slope angle (TSA) were measured by the proposed method. The KJA is defined as the angle between the femoral shaft axis and the patellar axis. The PH is defined as the distance between the most proximal and distal points of the patella. The PHR was calculated as the ratio of the PH to the length of the knee axis (J). The TSA is defined as the angle between the femoral shaft axis and the tibial shaft axis. The tibial shaft axis was defined as the line connecting the most proximal and distal points on the tibial plateau.

The definition of the center of the lumbar spine (central axis), the center of the sacro-iliac joint (SIJ), the center of the pelvic spine (PTS), and the center of the sacral spine (SSS). The SIJ is the midpoint of a line drawn between the sacral end plates of the S1 vertebra and the iliac wings. The PTS is the midpoint of a line drawn between the S1 and S2 vertebral bodies. The SSS is the midpoint of a line drawn between the sacral end plates of the S1 vertebra and the ischial tuberosities. The DHI is drawn as a line from the center of the lumbar spine (CC) to the center of the SIJ (SIS), and it is the midpoint of the line connecting the S1 and the SI2 vertebrae. The PI is the angle between the line from the center of the lumbar spine (CC) to the center of the SIJ (SIS) and the line from the center of the sacro-iliac joint (SIS) to the center of the sacral spine (SSS). The PT is the angle between the line from the center of the sacro-iliac joint (SIS) to the center of the sacral spine (SSS) and the line from the center of the sacro-iliac joint (SIS) to the center of the sacro-iliac joint (SIS).
